hints: Follow the chlorine atom through both equations and notice whether it is used up or remade at the end.
Count the outer shell electrons on a single Cl atom and recall what species with an unpaired electron is called.
Think about how UV light in the upper atmosphere splits the C-Cl bond in CFCs, by equal sharing or unequal sharing of electrons.
walkthrough:
**Check if Cl is a catalyst**

Look at the two equations together. Cl is used in the first step and remade in the second step.

$$\text{Cl} + \text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{O}_2 + \text{ClO}$$
$$\text{ClO} + \text{O} \rightarrow \text{Cl} + \text{O}_2$$
Overall, Cl is not consumed, but it speeds up ozone breakdown. That is exactly what a catalyst does, so statement 1 is correct.

**Check if Cl is a free radical**

A chlorine atom has 7 outer electrons, so it has one unpaired electron: $\text{Cl}^{\bullet}$.

Any atom or molecule with an unpaired electron is a free radical. So statement 2 is correct.

**Check how Cl is formed from CFCs**

In the upper atmosphere, UV radiation breaks the C-Cl bond in chlorofluorocarbons.

$$\text{C-Cl} \rightarrow \text{C}^{\bullet} + \text{Cl}^{\bullet}$$
The bond breaks evenly, one electron goes to each atom. This is homolytic fission, not heterolytic fission which would make ions. So statement 3 is incorrect.

**Combine the conclusions**

Statements 1 and 2 are correct, statement 3 is incorrect. Choose the option that lists 1 and 2 only.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three statements. Statements 1 and 2 are true, but statement 3 is false since CFCs release Cl by homolytic fission to give radicals, not heterolytic fission to give ions.
options.B: Correct because it includes 1 and 2 only. Cl is regenerated so it acts as a catalyst, and Cl with one unpaired electron is a free radical. Statement 3 is correctly left out.
options.C: Incorrect because it includes statement 3 and leaves out statement 1. Statement 3 is wrong (homolytic, not heterolytic fission) and statement 1 is true and should be included.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes statement 1 only. Statement 1 is true, but statement 2 is also true and is missed out. A Cl atom is a classic free radical.
